title: Assemble landing page with data fetching and subscriptions
description:
Replace `dashboard/frontend/app/page.tsx` (currently a redirect to Mission Control) with the landing page.

1. Import and use `LANDING_VIEW_QUERY` with the project's GraphQL client hook (useQuery or equivalent).
2. Import `RESPOND_TO_ESCALATION_MUTATION` and create a mutation handler.
3. Import the existing `TASK_STATUS_SUBSCRIPTION` and subscribe for live Execute panel updates.
4. Wire connection state from the subscription client to StatusBar's `connected` prop.
5. Compose the page:
   ```
   <TopBar projectName={data.projectName} branch={data.branch} />
   <EditorialGrid
     definePanel={<DefinePanel {...data.define} />}
     judgePanel={<JudgePanel judge={data.judge} narrative={data.narrative} />}
     executePanel={<ExecutePanel execute={data.execute} onRespondToEscalation={handleEscalation} />}
     learnPanel={<LearnPanel {...data.learn} />}
   />
   <StatusBar ... />
   ```
6. Loading state: render a skeleton grid (same T-shape with pulsing placeholders) while query loads.
7. Error state: render the grid with empty panels and a top-level error banner.
8. After escalation mutation succeeds, refetch the landing view query to update panels.
9. On subscription event for taskStatusChanged, refetch the landing view query.

spec_references.requirement: S1: see all four phases simultaneously when opening the dashboard
dashboard/frontend/app/page.tsx: Replace redirect with landing page component
Single summary resolver — one query aggregates all four panels
Live updates via taskStatusChanged subscription for Execute panel

rationale: The page is the integration point for all panel components, data fetching, and subscriptions. Requires opus because it coordinates six component imports, query/mutation/subscription wiring, and three render states (loading/error/data). Depends on all panel and layout component tasks.
assumptions: Replacing the root redirect is the chosen approach per Q1 — Mission Control will be accessible via sidebar nav
Single query refetch is acceptable for subscription-triggered updates (no partial panel refresh)
decisions: Used module-level variable to capture onRespondToEscalation handler from the mocked ExecutePanel, avoiding fragile dynamic import patterns for mutation testing
Mocked all child components (TopBar, EditorialGrid, panels, StatusBar, Skeleton) to isolate page-level logic from component internals
Used color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-red) 8%, transparent) for ErrorBanner background so it stays in sync if --color-red changes
concerns: Tests are written for vitest + @testing-library/react which are not yet in package.json — they will not run until task 19 wires up the test framework (same situation as all other component tests)
The undeclared file scope warning for page.test.tsx is cosmetic, consistent with all other tasks' test files
